The story's own prediction held on essentially every file: a hand-written type restating a table hid something real. Roughly forty live defects came out with the backlog. The ones worth knowing about:
- Pricing.tsx sent `priceId.replace('monthly','yearly')` to checkout, so choosing Yearly charged the MONTHLY price. subscription_plans has stripe_price_id_monthly/_yearly and get_stripe_price_id() to choose between them; the hand-written SubscriptionPlan listed 5 of 16 columns and hid all of it. NOT verified against live Stripe — worth a manual checkout test.
- Adding a testimonial from the dashboard always failed: the form is camelCase and went straight into an insert, so it named columns that do not exist and omitted NOT NULL client_name.
- SocialShareDialog threw a temporal-dead-zone ReferenceError on open and had never rendered once.
- The listing-description tool's paywall never engaged (isUnlocked vs isLocked), so every visitor got all four descriptions without giving an email; EmailCaptureModal also recorded listingId: undefined on the leads it did get.
- FullProfilePage's JSON-LD Review nodes read author/content, not columns, so every review went to Google as "Anonymous" with no body.
- Four of five web vitals were never reported: onFID was removed in web-vitals v4 and threw into a silent catch before CLS/TTFB/INP registered.
- URL-imported listings discarded every scraped photo.
- The admin user list showed every subscription as "none" (plan vs plan_name).
- CompetitorMatrix ordered by a column that does not exist, so its query always errored into a swallowed catch; its three insight cards could never render anyway, reading five non-columns.
- LinkStack custom_css was passed as {cssText}, which React ignores, so it never applied.
- The leads report exported a Score column of zeroes; ListingsBlock rendered prices as "$$450,000"; QuickActionsDashboard showed every listing as $0.
- About a dozen new Date(nullable) sites rendering the Unix epoch as "1/1/1970" or "over 56 years ago".

FIVE hand-written Profile types existed; there is now one, derived from the generated Row, and the same was done for Listing, Testimonial, Lead, Article, SSOConfig, SubscriptionPlan and the SEO admin panels' rows.

METHOD NOTE for future work of this kind: deriving four admin panels' types in one pass took the count 87 -> 126, because each honest type surfaces its own cluster of nullable-column work. Derive ONE type, drive that file to zero, then move on.

FOUND BUT OUT OF SCOPE, each wants its own story:
(1) The schema has a `lead_scores` table (score, probability, confidence, priority, model_version, feature_importance, keyed by lead_id) and NOTHING in src/ or supabase/functions/ reads or writes it. ML scoring is computed client-side per render and persisted nowhere, so scores cannot be queried or compared over time.
(2) Nothing writes seo_competitor_analysis at all — refreshAnalysis is an explicit stub — so CompetitorKeywordGap in CompetitorMatrix.tsx is a contract a future writer must satisfy, not a shape observed in data.
(3) AddTestimonialModal collects a clientPhoto File that nothing uploads; client_photo stores a URL and is left null.

userStories.notes: DONE 2026-08-06 in migration 20260806000003_pin_security_definer_search_path.sql. All 50 pinned via ALTER FUNCTION rather than rewriting bodies, so there is no chance of a transcription error in the logic and the migration is idempotent for the CI three-pass loop. Pin is `public, extensions, pg_temp`, not bare `public`: pgcrypto and uuid-ossp live in `extensions` both locally and on hosted Supabase, and generate_encryption_key() calls gen_random_bytes(), so a bare public pin would have broken it -- confirmed by calling it after the pin. pg_temp is named last precisely so it is searched last instead of first, which is the actual attack. The two functions already pinned (search_path=public and search_path=public, auth) were left alone. Demonstrated both ways on a clone of log_audit_event: unpinned, an authenticated attacker's `CREATE TEMP TABLE audit_logs` captured the audit row (temp=1, real=0) -- the audit trail silently diverted; pinned, the same attack captured nothing and the row reached the real table (temp=0, real=1). Crypto moved into a new `pii-crypto` Edge Function holding PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY; src/lib/pii.ts is now a thin client that cannot decrypt anything on its own, which is the point. VITE_PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY is gone from src/lib/pii.ts, .env.example and DEPLOYMENT.md's env table. Existing ciphertext survives: supabase/functions/_shared/encryption.ts already produced a byte-identical envelope to the old client (same enc:v1: prefix, PBKDF2-SHA256 at 100k iterations, 16-byte salt prepended to the 12-byte IV, base64-of-JSON), verified by reading both implementations side by side. So the migration is carrying the key across, not re-keying -- DEPLOYMENT.md §2.1 documents setting the function secret to the current VITE_PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY value, then removing it from Cloudflare Pages. Rotation is written up as a separate job needing a decrypt-old/re-encrypt-new backfill, and is the reason the plaintext columns should not retire until after it. Batched rather than per-value, or the leads list would have been two round trips per row: pii.ts gains encryptPIIBatch/decryptPIIBatch, useLeads decrypts a whole page in two calls and encrypts both fields in one, and values needing no work (empty, or lacking the enc:v1: prefix) short-circuit locally so an all-plaintext page makes no request at all. The function requires a JWT and is rate limited per user rather than per IP (agents behind one office NAT should not share a budget); confirmed check_rate_limit takes p_identifier text so a `user:<uuid>` key works. Encrypt fails closed, decrypt fails open. Found and removed an adjacent instance of the same defect while checking for leftovers: src/hooks/useEncryption.ts had zero callers and read VITE_ENCRYPTION_SECRET with a hardcoded fallback default -- another bundled key, one import away from being picked up. Deleted along with its env var. src/lib/encryption.ts is kept (pure primitives that take the secret as an argument and read no env var, plus its tests guard the envelope the edge function must stay compatible with) with a header note saying so. pii.test.ts rewritten against a stubbed edge function, covering position preservation, the local short-circuits, and both failure directions: 14 tests, suite total 274 -> 277. tsc unchanged at 321, eslint 0 errors, build and verify:schema green.

userStories.title: Unauthenticated SSRF in seven URL-fetching edge functions
userStories.description: crawl-site, check-broken-links, check-security-headers, detect-redirect-chains, analyze-images, check-core-web-vitals and check-mobile-first all take a caller-supplied URL, pass it through new URL() — which parses, it does not validate — and fetch it. No scheme check, no private-range or link-local block, no allow-list. http://169.254.169.254/ and http://127.0.0.1:<port>/ are both reachable, from a process holding the service-role key, with the response body returned to the caller. _shared/url-validation.ts exists but only covers redirect URLs for SSO; there is no SSRF guard in the codebase. All seven are also unauthenticated (US-078).
acceptanceCriteria: A shared guard in _shared/ rejects any URL that is not http/https, resolves to a private, loopback, link-local or unique-local address, or names a metadata endpoint
The guard resolves DNS and checks the resolved address, so a hostname pointing at 127.0.0.1 is rejected too
All seven functions call it before any fetch, including on redirect hops (detect-redirect-chains follows Location headers)
Requests for 169.254.169.254, 127.0.0.1, 10.0.0.0/8 and a public hostname with a private A record are all rejected — verified by executing the functions
A legitimate public URL still crawls successfully
userStories.notes: DONE 2026-08-08. New supabase/functions/_shared/ssrf-guard.ts, wired into all seven. safeFetch() replaces bare fetch() in crawl-site, check-broken-links, check-security-headers, detect-redirect-chains, analyze-images and check-mobile-first; check-core-web-vitals hands the URL to Google's PageSpeed API rather than fetching it, so it validates the input instead — a private address there cannot reach our network but is still a request we should not make on someone's behalf, and it leaks internal hostnames to a third party. The guard blocks non-http(s) schemes, localhost/.internal, and the private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT, multicast and reserved ranges — and, importantly, RESOLVES the hostname and checks the answer, because internal.example.com with an A record of 10.0.0.5 defeats any string check. It re-checks every redirect hop, since a public URL that 302s to 127.0.0.1 defeats a single up-front check. One subtlety found while wiring it: detect-redirect-chains passes redirect: manual and walks the chain itself to report every hop, and safeFetch following redirects internally would have consumed exactly what that function exists to show — safeFetch now honours an explicit manual redirect, guarding the URL and returning the single response, with per-hop safety preserved because the caller comes back through it. 6 tests cover the address matching, including IPv4-mapped IPv6 (::ffff:127.0.0.1) and the ranges either side of the private blocks (172.15/172.32, 192.167/192.169) so an over-broad prefix check would fail. Running them needed vitest.config.ts extended to include supabase/functions/**/*.test.ts — CI only ran deno check over that tree, which type-checks but executes nothing, so pure logic there had no test at all. RESIDUAL, NOT CLOSED: DNS rebinding. The name is resolved here and again by fetch(), and a hostile resolver can answer differently; closing it needs connect-time pinning that Deno's fetch does not expose.

userStories.title: Stripe hardening: real rate limiting, durable idempotency, and a fail-closed plan default
userStories.description: Three defects in the billing path. (1) There are two rate limiters: _shared/rate-limiter.ts is DB-backed via rpc('check_rate_limit'), _shared/rateLimit.ts is a module-level Map — useless across ephemeral horizontally-scaled isolates — and the in-memory one is the one guarding create-checkout-session, create-portal-session, create-stripe-customer and report-stripe-usage. (2) stripe-webhook keeps processed event IDs in a module-level Map, so Stripe's retries land on cold instances and reprocess; the module-scope setInterval also pins the isolate for no benefit. (2) Webhook idempotency is now a stripe_processed_events table with the event id as primary key, and the unique constraint IS the check — an insert that conflicts means the event is already handled, which is race-free in a way the old read-then-write Map was not even in principle. The claim fails OPEN on any error other than 23505: Stripe retries, and processing an event twice is far less damaging than dropping a subscription change. The module-scope setInterval sweeper is gone with it. (3) getPlanNameFromPriceId ended `|| 'professional'`, so any price id not in the hardcoded map or the STRIPE_PRICE_* env vars — a new tier, an add-on, a typo — silently granted professional entitlements. userStories.description: signInWithPassword completes and issues a full session before any second factor is considered (useAuthStore.ts:318-377). requiresMFA is ordinary Zustand state and MFAChallenge sets mfaVerified on success, so someone with the password and no TOTP already holds a working access_token: they can call PostgREST directly, or run useAuthStore.setState({ mfaVerified: true }). acceptanceCriteria: MFA uses Supabase's native enrol/challenge/verify so that the second factor determines the session's AAL

userStories.notes:
IN PROGRESS 2026-09-01. Client-side native MFA is implemented; the RLS enforcement is written but DELIBERATELY NOT APPLIED. Scope was agreed with the user: implement the flow, hold back the part that can lock people out until it can be verified against a real GoTrue.

WHAT IS DONE:
- src/hooks/useNativeMFA.ts: enrol / challenge / verify / unenroll through supabase.auth.mfa, plus a status read from getAuthenticatorAssuranceLevel() + listFactors() so the client's view of MFA comes from the token rather than from local state.
- useAuthStore.signIn: requiresMFA now derives from the token's AAL (nextLevel === 'aal2' && currentLevel === 'aal1'), not from a user_mfa_settings boolean. The flags drive ROUTING only — setState({mfaVerified:true}) no longer buys access to anything once the RLS below is applied.
- getSecurityContext (lib/security/authentication.ts): the hardcoded `isMFAVerified = true` with its 'For now, assume verified if they got past login' comment is gone. It reads the real AAL, and on any error it fails CLOSED rather than defaulting to verified. SecureRoute's requireMFA prop consumes this and therefore does something now.
- NativeMFAVerification / NativeMFASettings components, wired into /auth/mfa and dashboard Settings.

EXISTING ENROLLED USERS — the migration path, which the notes asked to be planned first. The old TOTP secret CANNOT be transplanted: it is encrypted with PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY inside the Edge Function, and Supabase has no supported write path into auth.mfa_factors other than mfa.enroll(), which mints its own secret. So re-enrolment is unavoidable. It is authorised by the OLD factor (useNativeMFA.migrateLegacyFactor): the user enters their current code, it is checked through the legacy verify-mfa function, and only then is the native factor enrolled and the legacy row disabled. A password alone can never enrol a replacement. Nobody is locked out, and both systems are live only for the length of each user's own transition.

NOT DONE — and this is the half that provides the actual protection:
supabase/migrations/pending/20260901000002_require_aal2_for_mfa_users.sql adds a mfa_satisfied() predicate to the SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE policies on leads and to SELECT on subscriptions/user_subscriptions. It is in pending/ because supabase/migrations/*.sql is a non-recursive glob, so neither CI nor `supabase db push` picks it up. Applying it BEFORE the client changes ship and users have re-enrolled locks out every enrolled agent, since nothing will have upgraded their session to aal2. The preconditions and the query for counting un-migrated users are in supabase/migrations/pending/README.md.

LEGACY UI REMOVED: useMFA, MFASetup, MFASettings and MFAVerification are deleted. Once the native flow landed nothing referenced them — they formed a closed island pointing at the old backend — and keeping them would have left two MFA UIs live against two systems, which is what this story's note warns against. Only the Edge Functions remain: setup-mfa is now unused, and verify-mfa / disable-mfa are still called by the re-enrolment bridge. Retire all three, plus user_mfa_settings / mfa_temp_codes / mfa_trusted_devices / mfa_verification_logs, once the enrolled count above reaches zero.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA STATUS:
1. Native enrol/challenge/verify determines AAL — DONE (code), UNVERIFIED (no GoTrue available locally).
2. Pre-challenge token cannot read own leads via direct PostgREST — NOT MET. Requires the pending migration, and needs executing with a real pre-challenge token to prove.
3. RLS on lead and subscription tables requires aal2 — WRITTEN, NOT APPLIED.
4. getSecurityContext reports real MFA state and requireMFA does something — DONE.
5. Existing users migrated without lockout — DESIGNED AND IMPLEMENTED, UNVERIFIED.
6. npm run test:run passes — DONE (304 passed; tsc 0 errors, build passes, verify:schema passes).

TESTS: src/lib/security/mfa-assurance.test.ts covers every branch of how isMFAVerified is derived — no factor, enrolled-but-unchallenged, enrolled-and-challenged, legacy enrolment, and the error path. That last one matters most: the old code defaulted to VERIFIED on any error, and 'fails closed' is a claim worth holding to a test. The enrol/challenge round trip itself is still uncovered — it needs a real GoTrue.

NEXT STEP for whoever picks this up: stand up a staging Supabase, exercise enrol -> sign out -> sign in -> challenge, confirm the JWT carries aal2, then execute criterion 2 explicitly with a captured pre-challenge token before promoting the pending migration.

userStories.title: PII encryption on leads is defence-in-depth theatre
userStories.description: leads.encrypted_email and encrypted_phone are dual-written by useLeads.ts:78, but the plaintext email and phone columns are still populated on the same row under the same RLS, so the ciphertext protects nothing an attacker could not already read. submit-lead — the path every public capture should use — writes no encrypted columns at all, so coverage is inconsistent as well as ineffective. gdpr-export/index.ts:174 already carries a TODO to decrypt on read.
acceptanceCriteria: Either the plaintext columns are dropped and every reader decrypts (useLeads already has the read path), or the encrypted columns are dropped and the feature stops being described as encryption at rest
Whichever direction is chosen is applied consistently across useLeads, submit-lead and gdpr-export
Existing rows are backfilled or migrated, not left in a mixed state
gdpr-export returns readable contact details for the data subject
npm run verify:schema passes
userStories.notes:
DONE 2026-09-01. Chose the option the story names as the only real one: the plaintext leads.email/leads.phone columns are dropped and every reader decrypts.

The cost objection in the original note ('every query that filters or sorts on email/phone has to change, and search over encrypted columns is not free') turned out not to apply. Nothing filters or sorts on those columns in SQL: there is no .ilike/.eq against leads.email or leads.phone anywhere in src/ or supabase/functions/, and the one lead search (dashboard/Leads.tsx) runs client-side over rows useLeads has already decrypted. So the honest option was also the cheap one.

Applied consistently across all four paths the story names:
- useLeads: encrypted-only on insert and update (was dual-writing); read path already decrypted.
- submit-lead: now encrypts before insert. This was the real coverage hole — the path every public capture form uses wrote NO ciphertext at all.
- gdpr-export: now decrypts for the subject's own copy, closing the TODO at index.ts:174. A subject access request that returned ciphertext would not be an export.
- sample-data-service: now encrypts.
- useSecureLeads: deleted. It had no callers and never decrypted, so reviving it would have shown ciphertext in the UI.
- useAnalytics: selects encrypted_* and decrypts, because LeadsTable renders email and phone.

MIGRATION SAFETY. The AES key lives only in the Edge Function secrets (US-066), so no SQL can encrypt and the backfill has to be a function: supabase/functions/backfill-lead-pii (admin-only, idempotent, batched). 20260901000001_leads_drop_plaintext_pii.sql counts rows that still hold plaintext with no ciphertext and RAISES rather than dropping. Verified both branches against a real Postgres: with an un-backfilled row it refuses and the email survives; after backfill it drops cleanly. Order is documented in DEPLOYMENT.md §2.2.

OPERATIONAL RISK, stated plainly in DEPLOYMENT.md: PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY is now the ONLY way to read a lead's contact details. There is no plaintext column to reconstruct from any more, which also means key rotation must decrypt under the old key first. The previous §2.1 text said retiring these columns should wait until after any rotation for exactly that reason; that trade is now made deliberately and written down rather than left implicit.

VERIFIED: npm run verify:schema passes (all 12 checks — it caught three real integration points during this work: the check's own insert, useAnalytics' select, and the backfill's pre-drop read). types.ts regenerated from the migrated schema and `types:check` reports it in sync. npx tsc --noEmit 0 errors. npm run test:run 298 passed. npm run build passes.

NOT VERIFIED: nothing here has run against the live database. The backfill function has not been executed, and the migration has only been applied to a local Postgres built from supabase/migrations. Run the DEPLOYMENT.md §2.2 sequence in a staging environment before production.

NOTE for whoever picks up US-085: deriving Lead from the row surfaced the same class of defect US-056 kept finding — leads.created_at and leads.status are nullable, and Leads.tsx treated an undated lead as breaching the SLA (new Date(null) is the epoch), while useMLLeadScoring put it at hour 0 on a Thursday and skewed its time-of-day features. Both fixed here.

userStories.title: Account deletion fails outright, and would orphan tenant data if it did not
userStories.description: Found while verifying US-083. process_scheduled_account_deletions() performs DELETE FROM auth.users, which raises: insert or update on table "audit_logs" violates foreign key constraint "audit_logs_actor_id_fkey". So a GDPR right-to-erasure request is accepted, scheduled, the 30-day grace period elapses, and the job then errors forever. Separately, even once the delete succeeds it would not erase much: leads, listings, testimonials, user_settings, article_webhooks and analytics_views have no foreign key on user_id at all, so nothing cascades to them. Those rows carry lead names, emails and phone numbers.

REPRODUCED FIRST. The call rate-limiter.ts made, executed against the applied schema:
  SELECT * FROM check_rate_limit(p_ip_address => '1.2.3.4', p_endpoint => 'submit-lead', ...);
  ERROR: function public.check_rate_limit(p_ip_address => unknown, p_endpoint => unknown, ...) does not exist
The correct names return a row: t|4|<reset_at>. So the limiter errored on every call in all thirteen functions and the error branch returned allowed: true.

ORIGIN, worth recording because it explains the shape of the bug: p_ip_address and p_endpoint are the COLUMN names of public.rate_limits — an orphaned table from an earlier design that nothing has written to since. check_rate_limit reads and writes rate_limit_entries (identifier, limit_type). The limiter's own header comment said "rate_limits table", which is how the wrong names looked right.

FIXES:
1. rate-limiter.ts sends p_identifier / p_limit_type / p_max_requests / p_window_seconds.
2. RateLimitConfig gains failClosed. submission and auth set it true — for those an unavailable limiter means no control on abuse at all — general stays open so a read endpoint does not go down over a transient DB fault. Also set on generate-article's ad-hoc config, whose own comment says the limit exists to cap a model bill. gdpr-export's is deliberately left open: refusing a data-subject request is worse than allowing a second export in an hour. Every path now logs the PostgREST message at error level with "failing open"/"failing closed"; the old code logged error?.message and returned allowed: true for everything, which is how a call that never once succeeded went unnoticed.
3. Migration 20260902000002 repoints cleanup_rate_limits() at rate_limit_entries (deleting on window_end, the column check_rate_limit maintains) with search_path pinned. It had been deleting from rate_limits, so it ran successfully, removed nothing, and rate_limit_entries grew without bound. The orphan table is left in place — dropping it belongs with US-124 — but nothing references it now.

VERIFY:SCHEMA — two new checks, both demonstrated to fail on the original defect:
- "every rpc() call's named arguments exist on the function" reads pg_proc.proargnames, filtered by proargmodes to input parameters only (proargnames includes OUT columns, so an unfiltered list would have accepted a call passing `allowed` as an argument). Restoring p_ip_address/p_endpoint makes it FAIL and exit 1, naming the file and listing what the function accepts. The scanner is depth- and ternary-aware: nested objects (p_details: { count: n }) and conditionals (p_action: cond ? 'a' : 'b') were both producing false positives across every log_audit_event call in the tree. Non-literal argument objects, spreads and computed keys are reported as notes rather than guessed at.
- "check_rate_limit refuses the 11th call in a window" runs ten calls at a limit of ten, asserts each is allowed with remaining counting 9..0, asserts the eleventh returns false,0, then expires the row and asserts cleanup_rate_limits() collects it. Reverting the cleanup fix makes it FAIL with "cleanup_rate_limits() left an expired rate_limit_entries row behind".

(1) NO CONTACT DETAILS. notify-lead passed lead.email and lead.phone — columns 20260901000001 dropped — so the agent's New Lead email read "Email: undefined" and the HTML contact rows were filtered out. It now decrypts encrypted_email / encrypted_phone through _shared/encryption.ts decryptSecret() before rendering.

Worth noting what went with it: the inline HTML interpolated the visitor's name and message unescaped, which the shared createLeadNotificationEmail template does not.

(3) PREFERENCES. notify-lead skipped anything that was not 'instant', so every agent on 'daily_digest' was never emailed about a lead at all — there is no digest job. 'off' now suppresses; 'daily_digest' sends instantly, which is the failure mode that loses no leads. Said plainly in the settings UI: the option reads "Not available yet — currently sends instantly, like Instant" rather than "One summary email per day". Two stale `as never` / `as {...}` casts in that component are gone too — notification_preferences has been in types.ts throughout (types.ts:3414), same pattern as US-094.

(4) THE TRIGGER THAT NEVER FIRED. Confirmed against the applied schema: after every migration, current_setting('app.settings.functions_url', true) is NULL, so notify_lead_on_insert() returned early every time. Migration 20260902000003 drops the trigger and the function. It is not repaired because the documented setup stores the service-role key as a plaintext GUC readable through any SECURITY DEFINER function — worse than the notification being broken. trg_notify_new_lead / notify_new_lead() are a different trigger, take no GUCs, insert the in-app notifications row, and are untouched.

(5) SENDEMAIL. Returns { ok, providerId, error } instead of void. A missing RESEND_API_KEY is an error in production (a warning elsewhere, so local dev needs no key), a non-2xx from Resend reports the status and body, a network error reports its message — none of them throw, so a notification failure still cannot roll back the lead. notify-lead logs audit status 'success'/'failure' from the actual result rather than unconditionally.

(6) TIMELINE. Every agent notification writes a lead_activities row of activity_type 'email' with the subject and recipient, titled for success or failure. Verified against the schema that the insert is accepted and sits alongside the existing 'form_submission' activity. A failed send now also returns 502 rather than 200.

DEVIATION — useLeads does NOT call notify-lead, and the criterion asked it to. Two reasons, both stated rather than worked around: notify-lead notifies leads.user_id, so on this path it would email an agent about a lead they had just typed into their own CRM; and reaching it from the browser means accepting a user session on a function US-078 deliberately restricted to the service role.   SELECT log_lead_call('<lead>', 'connected', 120, 'Talked through budget');
  ERROR: column "last_contacted_at" of relation "leads" does not exist
  CONTEXT: PL/pgSQL function log_lead_call(uuid,text,integer,text) line 40
The activity row is inserted before that UPDATE, so the exception rolled back both — the agent would log a call and lose the call and the timestamp together.

CORRECTION TO THE STORY'S PREMISE. It says "nothing in src/ calls them yet". src/hooks/useLeadActivities.ts calls all three (lines 139, 163, 188, 213). What is true is that no component imports that hook, so there is no reachable caller — the defect is latent because the UI is not wired up, not because the call sites do not exist. US-102 mounts it, which is still the reason this had to land first.

MIGRATION 20260902000004 rewrites all three to set contacted_at, using COALESCE(contacted_at, NOW()) rather than NOW(). The column records FIRST contact — Leads.tsx measures response time from it and the SLA card keys off it — so overwriting it on every follow-up would make an agent look faster the more often they called. Verified: all three now return an activity id, the timeline shows call/email/meeting/note alongside the trigger's form_submission, contacted_at is set, and a second call leaves it unchanged.

EXECUTE-WORKFLOW. The update_lead node did `if (score) updates.score = score` against `leads`, which has no score column, so a workflow setting a score also failed to apply the status and notes beside it. It now upserts lead_scores (lead_id, user_id, score, priority, variant, scored_at) on the lead_id unique constraint, reading user_id from the lead rather than trusting workflow context, clamping the score to the 0-100 CHECK, deriving priority within the hot/warm/cold CHECK, and recording variant 'rules' — a workflow-set score is a rule, not a model prediction.

NOTIFY-LEAD read lead.score ?? lead.lead_score, neither of which exists, so the score badge never rendered. It now reads lead_scores.score with maybeSingle(); a missing row is normal (scoring may not have run) and renders no badge.

VERIFY:SCHEMA — two new checks, 15 -> 16 total, both demonstrated against the original defect:
- "plpgsql function bodies reference only real columns" parses UPDATE ... SET and INSERT INTO ... (cols) targets out of every plpgsql body in public, not just trigger functions, which is the gap that let this through. Restoring the broken UPDATE makes it FAIL with "log_lead_call: UPDATE leads SET last_contacted_at — no such column", exit 1. Conservative by design: only tables the catalog knows and simple column lists are checked, and a body that defeats the parse is skipped rather than guessed at.
- "log_lead_activity / _call / _email run against a real lead" executes all three as the owning user against a fixture lead, asserts the three activity types land, asserts contacted_at is set, and asserts a later call does not move it. A body parse cannot see an ownership guard that never passes or a CHECK constraint; this can. Confirmed it fails with the original ERROR when the broken function is restored.

An effect keyed on lead.id now re-initialises status, note, notes and selectedResponse. Worth stating plainly: the consequence was not only a wrong badge — saving from that state wrote one lead's note onto another.

(2) CONTACT ACTIONS, both surfaces. The mailto:/tel:/sms: links had no side effect, so an agent who phoned a lead a minute after it arrived still read "No response · 3h". src/hooks/useLeadContactAction.ts holds the behaviour and is used by the detail modal AND the Leads page card, so the two cannot drift: a 'new' lead moves to 'contacted' with contacted_at set, and the timeline row goes through log_lead_call / log_lead_email / log_lead_activity. The link is never intercepted — the href fires and the dialer opens — and a failure to record is logged without blocking the call. On the card the click also stopPropagation()s, which it did not before: tapping a phone number used to open the detail modal behind the dialer.

CallOutcome gained 'initiated'. The existing four (answered/voicemail/no_answer/busy) are outcomes an agent reports afterwards; tapping tel: establishes only that the dialer opened, and recording 'answered' would put a fact in the timeline nobody established. There is no CHECK constraint on lead_activities.call_outcome.

When no lead row is supplied — the bulk action holds none — the rules depending on the previous value are skipped rather than guessed at, while the clearing rules still apply.

(4) RESPONSE TIME. Verified against the applied schema, the whole cycle: a 'new' lead updated with the contact patch gets first_responded_at from set_lead_first_responded_at; converting sets closed_at; the reset-to-'new' patch clears all three (the trigger does not fire, since NEW.status = 'new'); and a subsequent move to 'contacted' sets first_responded_at again. That last step never worked — a reopened lead kept a first_responded_at the trigger could never re-set, so it counted as responded to forever and could never contribute to the KPI again.

userStories.notes:
DONE 2026-09-02. Frontend covered by tests; the scheduler's SQL verified against a real Postgres; the scheduler itself unverified end to end (no deployment here).

(1) NEXT STEP. src/lib/leadNextStep.ts narrows the advice to one action with a button behind it, rendered in the modal header. getRecommendedActions() had produced emoji strings since it was written and no component ever rendered them — a paragraph an agent must interpret is not guidance. An unanswered new lead outranks everything (call, or email when there is no phone number, with the wait time in the rationale); a lead quiet for 3+ days gets a follow-up; a hot score gets a viewing; a closed lead gets a referral check-in. Tapping the button opens the dialer/mail client AND records the response through useLeadContactAction; for a 'task' step it prefills the follow-up form rather than inventing a due date.

(2) FOLLOW-UP TASKS. lead_activities' task_due_date / task_priority / task_completed_at had never been written to. useLeadActivities gains createTask and completeTask; the modal has an inline "Add a follow-up" row with a due date and a Mark done button on each open task; and components/dashboard/DueFollowUps.tsx renders a "Due today" block on Overview from a new useDueLeadTasks query. Overdue tasks are shown alongside today's rather than disappearing once their date passes — a slipped reminder is the one that most needs surfacing. The block renders nothing when nothing is due.

(3) SLA_HOURS ON THE PROFILE. Was useState(2) in Leads.tsx. Now profiles.notification_preferences.sla_hours, edited in Settings ("Chase me about unanswered leads after"), read by the Leads page and by the scheduled job.

IMPORTANT: this nearly reintroduced US-094's bug. Adding a second consumer of notification_preferences meant two hooks with their own queryFn under one queryKey — exactly the ['leads'] collision where whichever mounts first decides the shape the other sees. Consolidated into a single useNotificationPreferences hook that both the Settings card and the Leads page go through; its update merges rather than replaces, so setting the SLA cannot clear the notification mode.

(4) THE SCHEDULER, which the repo had none of. supabase/functions/scheduled-maintenance is one service-role endpoint driven by .github/workflows/scheduled-maintenance.yml on an hourly cron (at :17 — the top of the hour is when every GitHub schedule fires at once). GitHub was chosen over pg_cron because the self-hosted Supabase has no such extension and this needs no new infrastructure. It runs seven independent tasks, each caught separately so one failure cannot stop the rest, returning 207 when any fails:
  - overdue_leads: finds status='new' with first_responded_at IS NULL past the AGENT'S OWN sla_hours, inserts a notifications row and sends one email. At most once per lead ever, enforced by checking for an existing lead_overdue notification containing that lead_id. Honours leads='off'. It casts the net at the SHORTEST configurable window and filters per agent afterwards — filtering at the longest would silently exclude every agent who chose a tighter one.
  - account_deletions: calls process-account-deletions, which had no caller at all, so a requested deletion sat in the queue indefinitely — a GDPR commitment nothing honoured.
  - the five cleanup_* functions, none of which had ever executed. All five verified callable against the applied schema.
The workflow fails loudly when its secrets are absent rather than going green having done nothing, which is the failure mode US-090 warns about.

(5) NOTIFICATION DEEP LINK. data.lead_id was written by the trigger and read by nobody. The dropdown now navigates to /dashboard/leads?lead=<id>, and Leads.tsx consumes the param, opens that lead and clears it from the URL so a later close does not reopen the modal. Overview's recent-lead rows are links to the same route; they were plain divs, so the one place an agent sees a new lead on the dashboard was a dead end.

(6) WORKFLOW NODES. create_task returned crypto.randomUUID() as a taskId and stored nothing — worse than failing, since the workflow looked like it created a follow-up and the agent was never reminded. It inserts a real task activity now, reading user_id from the lead where no assignee is given. send_sms is REMOVED, from the executor, the WorkflowActionSubtype union, NODE_CONFIG_SCHEMAS and the icon map: there is no SMS provider anywhere in this repo — no Twilio credentials, nothing in .env.example — and it was returning a sentAt timestamp for a message nobody sent.

VERIFICATION: npx tsc --noEmit 0 errors; npm run test:run 386 passed, 36 files (was 378); verify:schema 16/16; eslint 0 errors; the overdue query, the @> dedupe and all five cleanup RPCs executed against the applied schema; the workflow YAML parses. leadNextStep.test.ts adds 8 specs.

NOT VERIFIED, and it is the important gap: the scheduled job has never actually run. It needs the function deployed and SUPABASE_FUNCTIONS_URL / SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY set as repository secrets. Its SQL is verified; the HTTP path, the GitHub schedule firing, and the email send are not — same environmental blocker as US-090. Whoever deploys should run it once via workflow_dispatch and check the 200/207 body before trusting the hourly cron.

Beyond the CRM components in US-102: hooks useSecureListings (its VALID_STATUSES lacks under_contract and draft), useListingUpdate, useAutoSave, useLinkValidation and lib/image-seo.ts; MobileListingCard vs profile/ListingCard; components/LoadingSpinner.tsx vs ui/LoadingSpinner.tsx with SkeletonCard defined in both places; Hero3D.tsx and Hero3DPhone.tsx (react-three) while the rendered Hero3DShowpiece is CSS-only, yet three stays in deps and manualChunks; four sitemap implementations (pages/Sitemap.tsx, functions/sitemap, functions/generate-sitemap, static public/sitemap.xml); five static city pages superseded by DynamicLocationPage; RouterCheck, ReviewSchema, seo/PageSEO, seo/SchemaMarkup; five admin panels (AdminOperationsHub, ErrorLogViewer, MLLeadScoringDashboard, SystemHealthMonitor, UserManagementPanel), SubscriptionGuard, EnterpriseLogin and SSOConfigForm (mounted nowhere), useFeatureFlag/isFeatureEnabled with no consumer so flags control nothing, and the unused barrels pages/admin/index.ts and pages/dashboard/workflows/index.ts. Unused deps: axios, jsonwebtoken, @stripe/stripe-js, qrcode.react, react-dropzone, remark-gfm, three-mesh-bvh, tailwindcss-animate, @radix-ui/react-accordion, @radix-ui/react-toast; dev: workbox-build/precaching/routing/strategies, @vitejs/plugin-legacy, sharp, ts-node, @types/dompurify, @types/testing-library__jest-dom. TeamPage.tsx:35's 'teams aren't in the generated types' comment is stale and hides an any cast.
acceptanceCriteria: Every file knip lists as unused is deleted or wired, and knip runs in CI with the remaining allowlist committed
Feature flags either gate at least the SSO and workflows entry points or the table, manager and hook are removed together; SSO login/config are either routed or removed with their functions
One sitemap implementation remains and robots.txt points at it; one LoadingSpinner and one SkeletonCard
The listed dependencies are uninstalled; three is removed if Hero3D/Hero3DPhone go
npm run build, test:run and tsc pass; bundle size does not rise

userStories.title: Build output ships 17 MB of source maps to Cloudflare, two vendor chunks are over budget, and lint cannot fail
userStories.description: vite.config.ts sets sourcemap: 'hidden', which drops the sourceMappingURL comment but still emits 144 .map files into dist/assets (three-vendor 2.6 MB, index 1.66 MB); Cloudflare Pages uploads the whole of dist/, so the full source is fetchable by URL. dist is 26 MB, 17 MB of it maps. three-vendor is 820 KB and export-vendor 619 KB against the 600 KB vendor budget the file's own comment claims is enforced (the comment says 594; index is 466 KB against a noted 407). manualChunks hardcodes 14 Radix packages by name. eslint reports 726 warnings and 0 errors: react/no-unescaped-entities 343, @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any 251 (CLAUDE.md says no any), no-unused-vars 52, react-hooks/exhaustive-deps 21, no-empty-function 17, no-console 17. CI runs eslint --max-warnings=-1, which never fails on warnings, so the count is invisible and only rises.
acceptanceCriteria: Source maps are uploaded to Sentry in CI and deleted from dist/ before deploy (or sourcemap is false and the Sentry Vite plugin uploads them); a deployed build serves no .map file
check-bundle-size.mjs budgets are real and enforced; export-vendor is split or lazy so the PDF library loads only on export; the baseline comments in vite.config.ts are refreshed or removed
manualChunks routes node_modules/@radix-ui/* by prefix rather than by name
eslint runs in CI with --max-warnings set to the current count and the number is ratcheted down in each PR; no-explicit-any and exhaustive-deps are errors for new code via an overrides block
react/no-unescaped-entities is cleared with eslint --fix in one commit

userStories.title: Decide the fate of the SEO suite: 32 tables, 37 uncalled functions and 460 KB of admin UI that the agent never sees
userStories.description: Of 135 public tables, 32 are seo_* plus gsc_*, yandex_*, ga4_* and pseo_*; src/ queries 8 of the 32. Of 89 edge functions, 33 are invoked from src/ and 37 are referenced by nothing (analyze-*, check-*, crawl-site, detect-*, gsc-*, apply-seo-*, optimize-page-content, validate-structured-data, run-scheduled-audit and more), and no migration or workflow schedules any of them. 24 tables are touched by neither src/ nor supabase/functions (seo_automation_logs, seo_page_scores, seo_report_history, seo_settings, workflow_execution_queue, workflow_templates, workflow_triggers, workflow_versions, lead_scores, ml_training_examples, team_round_robin, rate_limits, mortgage_calculations, ...). src/components/admin is 460 KB across 33 components and SEODashboard.tsx is an 11-line wrapper around the same SEOManager that AdminDashboard.tsx:23 mounts as a tab. This is the platform's own marketing tooling living inside the agent product; it doubles the schema, the deno check surface and the migration risk for a product whose users are agents.
acceptanceCriteria: A written decision in docs/architecture: extract the SEO suite to its own repository, or keep it as an isolated src/admin-seo/ package with its own lazy entry and its own migration prefix
The 37 uninvoked functions are each either scheduled (US-103's scheduler), invoked from the admin UI, or deleted with their tables in a migration
The 24 orphan tables are dropped or claimed by a caller; verify:schema fails on a public table referenced by no code
/admin/seo is removed as a duplicate of the AdminDashboard tab
CLAUDE.md's table count and cluster description are updated

userStories.title: Advertised but unbuilt: URL import from Zillow, custom domains, and a first-run checklist that would replace them
userStories.description: Listings.tsx:403-406 offers 'Copy from Zillow, Realtor.com, etc.' and URLImportDialog.tsx:196-202 fakes a one-second load then errors 'Direct URL scraping requires a backend service'; photos is always [] (line 79). UpgradeModal.tsx:26,90-92 sells 'Connect your own domain' and useSubscriptionLimits.ts:11 gates custom_domain_enabled, but no component reads or writes profiles.custom_domain and no verification or Cloudflare hostname flow exists. Meanwhile the thing a new agent actually needs is missing: Overview.tsx:49 swaps the greeting for 48 hours, the copy-link block appears only inside the empty-leads card (196-213), there is no QR code anywhere (qrcode.react is installed and unused) and no setup checklist. Links.tsx/useSoftDelete cancel a pending delete on unmount so navigating away within 10 s silently keeps the link, visibleLinks memoises on a stable callback so the list never recomputes, and add/update/reorder toast twice. Testimonials.tsx shows Total Reviews twice, its empty-state button has no onClick, clientPhoto is never uploaded and edit cannot change is_featured.
acceptanceCriteria: The URL import mode is hidden until a scraper exists and the menu reads 'Paste listing text'; the custom-domain bullet is removed from UpgradeModal and the plan config until the feature ships
Overview shows a persistent setup checklist for new agents (add headshot, add first listing, copy your link, download QR code, share on Instagram) with a QR code generated from qrcode.react
Pending link deletes flush on unmount, the visible list recomputes on pendingCount, and each action toasts once
The Testimonials page shows each stat once, the empty-state button opens the add modal, client photos upload, and edit can toggle featured
